notes: This paper is a theoretical string theory study constraining the Type IIB string landscape using black hole superradiance observations. It does NOT present experimental exclusion limits on axion couplings (g_agamma, g_ae, etc.) in the conventional sense. Instead, it: (1) computes axion mass spectra and self-interactions (quartic couplings λ) for ~200,000 Calabi-Yau manifolds; (2) applies existing black hole superradiance constraints from astrophysical BH observations to exclude fractions of the CY3 landscape (e.g., ~50% at the tip of the Kähler cone, h1,1≈157). The exclusion is statistical over the landscape, not a direct coupling-vs-mass bound. Figure 2 shows example 2D exclusion regions in the (m_a, f_pert) plane for individual BHs, but no numerical (m, coupling) data points are extracted or tabulated. Figure 3 shows only the fraction of excluded manifolds vs Hodge number h1,1, with no coupling values. The paper does not provide extractable (mass, coupling) pairs suitable for a standard exclusion-limit database. This is a landscape-constraint paper, not an experimental dark matter search paper.
